### The Diamond of Grace on Black Velvet
Author: Adrian Rogers
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/loveworthfinding/love-worth-finding-july-9-2025.html
Passage: Judges 11:1
Points:
- Jephthah came from a painful and dishonorable background, yet God chose to use him mightily.
- Difficult origins can serve as the dark velvet background that accentuates the brilliance of divine grace.
- The Lord frequently humbles His servants through hardship before exalting them to leadership.
- Christians must refuse to live as victims of past circumstances and instead trust God to redeem their lives.

### A Message for Misfits
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/day-by-day-sept-18-2009-11607801.html
Passage: Judges 11:1-11
Points:
- Disowned and driven away by his legitimate brothers, Jephthah grew up an outcast and led an outlaw band.
- When facing destruction by the Ammonites, the elders of Gilead were forced to humble themselves and seek Jephthah's help.
- God's grace delights in taking broken, rejected misfits and shaping them into instruments of deliverance.
- Every believer shares Jephthah's story of being rescued from spiritual ruin purely through God's unmerited favor.

### Jephthah Rises to Lead Israel
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/jephthah-rises-to-lead-israel
Passage: Judges 11:9
Points:
- The elders of Gilead turned to the rejected warrior Jephthah to deliver them from severe Ammonite oppression.
- Jephthah engaged in diplomacy first, setting forth historical and theological arguments for Israel's right to the land.
- God delivered His people not because their repentance was flawless, but out of His tender compassion for their misery.
- Believers must look beyond the adequacy of their own repentance and rely wholly on the Lord's steadfast mercy.

### Bible Pathways - Mar. 26, 2008
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-mar-26-2008-11571642.html
Passage: Judges 11:1
Points:
- Despite being unjustly exiled by his clan into a foreign land, Jephthah kept his faith in the God of Israel.
- Human judgment looks at outward lineage and prestige, but God evaluates the sincerity and readiness of the heart.
- Long seasons of rejection and obscurity often serve as God's preparation ground for future ministry and leadership.
- In times of great crisis, God vindicated Jephthah's faithfulness by making him the leader his people desperately needed.
